R226.note: Asserts token.Method is *jwt.SigningMethodHMAC inside keyFunc before returning the secret, closing algorithm substitution; nothing else in the middleware changes.

R227.note: Correct pre-addition overflow guard (headerLen > UINT32_MAX - payloadLen) with no underflow risk; only the previously-UB overflow path now returns nullptr, legitimate calls are untouched.

R228.note: Authorization is keyed on the caller-supplied x-user-id metadata header, so any client can claim an owner/admin id, and the case's hand-written ServiceDesc handler never invokes the registered interceptor, so only the in-method check runs; it also invents users.is_admin and projects.owner_id columns and newly requires the header, so legitimate callers/schemas can start failing.

R229.note: Pins algorithms: ['RS256'] on jwt.verify, matching the documented issuance; error handling and response shape unchanged.

R230.note: HQL named parameter with the wildcards concatenated onto the bound value, preserving the original contains-match semantics exactly.

R231.note: Switches to length-prefixed RESP arrays, which makes CRLF in bio (and in the username-derived key) data rather than a command boundary; the SET/recv/close flow and return value are unchanged.

R232.note: JavaScriptEncoder.Default is the right encoder for a JS string literal (it escapes <, /, quotes and backslash to \uXXXX so Razor's subsequent HTML encoding is a no-op); title encoding and the numeric refreshSeconds are left as-is per the contract.

R233.note: Does not compile - dummyHash is declared string but assigned the []byte from bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword, so the whole auth package breaks; the intended logic (bcrypt hash at init, CompareHashAndPassword, dummy-hash path for unknown users) is otherwise behaviour-preserving for alice/hunter2.

R234.note: DynamicExpresso with reflection off closes the arbitrary-code path, but the method signature and the feature change (pasted C# rule classes with a named type and Evaluate method are no longer supported, and compile diagnostics are dropped), which breaks every existing caller - stated in the write-up but still stops legitimate use.

R235.note: Removes the is_staff widening so the list action matches IsTicketOwner, which the case docstring identifies as the intended sole rule; only nit is the docstring left verbatim still describing the removed staff widening as present.

R236.note: Positional ? placeholder with the wildcards inside the bound value is the correct ODBC parameterization (the @name in AddWithValue is ignored positionally, harmlessly); result shape and match semantics unchanged.

R237.note: Injects IAntiforgery and calls ValidateRequestAsync before the state change, which is the documented fix for JSON-bound minimal APIs; the failure path throws an unhandled AntiforgeryValidationException so a bad token yields a 500 rather than the 400 the write-up claims, but legitimate token-bearing callers are unaffected.

R238.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode applied to banner.Message at the sink, correct for the HTML text context; the trim/truncate pipeline, ContentType and timestamp formatting are unchanged.

R239.note: Both query-derived values are HtmlEncode'd at the point of interpolation; content type, markup and return value are otherwise identical.
